title: Divide a hundred, with the subclass caught first

blocks.text: Catch blocks are tried from top to bottom, so a subclass must be caught before its superclass. The types in one multi-catch must be unrelated.
Write `HundredDivider.describe(String input)`. It parses `input` as an `int` and divides `100` by it with integer division. It returns:
`NumberFormatException` is itself an `IllegalArgumentException`. And not every kind of division throws when the divisor is zero.

cases.says: It reports 100 divided by the value, in whole numbers.
A negative value is invalid input.
Text is reported as not a number: NumberFormatException is caught before its superclass IllegalArgumentException.
Zero is invalid input because integer division by zero throws; floating-point division would give Infinity instead.

concepts: Integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException, while floating-point division gives Infinity.
A subclass is caught before its superclass, so the more specific catch comes first.
